===== WORLD 25 · LESSON conditional_card_removal · Conditional card removal =====

TASK w25_1_teach [theory] What do you do before counting possible BB calls?
CAPTION: A blocker is a known card that removes combinations from a range. The useful comparison is between the combinations that survive in the relevant action group.
TEACH: What do you do before counting possible BB calls? A blocker is a known card that removes combinations from a range. The useful comparison is between the combinations that survive in the relevant action group.
Q: What do you do before counting possible BB calls?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
  + [correct] Remove board cards and your hole cards — Correct. A hand containing a known card cannot be in BB’s range.
  - [wrong] Remove the highest ranks first — Look again. A rank alone still has multiple cards.
    BETTER ANSWER: Remove board cards and your hole cards
  - [wrong] Remove hands sharing your kicker rank — Look again. Only direct card conflicts remove a combination.
    BETTER ANSWER: Remove board cards and your hole cards

TASK w25_1_read_one_pair_removal [drill] How many combinations remain?
CAPTION: Board Kc 9d 4s 3h 2c. Your hand contains Kh. Consider BB’s K-Q combinations with all suits allowed and neither player holding a known queen.
Q: How many combinations remain?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
  + [correct] 8 — Correct. Only Ks and Kd remain, and each can pair with any queen.
  - [wrong] 12 — Look again. That count removes the board king but retains your Kh.
    BETTER ANSWER: 8
  - [wrong] 4 — Look again. That treats an additional king as unavailable.
    BETTER ANSWER: 8

TASK w25_1_transfer_response_denominator [drill] How many folds survive in each denominator?
CAPTION: On study board Kh 9h 4h 7c 2s, a defender’s recorded range has AhQh, AhJh, QhJh, JhTh, KsQc and KdJd. The kings fold to the proposed bet. Compare Ac5s with Ah5s.
Q: How many folds survive in each denominator?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
REASONING: principle combos_and_blockers · alt alternative · edge processRule · stack_matters false · assumption On study board Kh 9h 4h 7c 2s, a defender’s recorded range has AhQh, AhJh, QhJh, JhTh, KsQc and KdJd. The kings fold to the proposed bet. Compare Ac5s with Ah5s.
  + [correct] Ac5s has 2/6; Ah5s has 2/4 — Correct. Ah removes two callers, while both king folds survive.
  - [wrong] Both have 2/6 — Look again. The AhQh and AhJh holdings cannot coexist with your Ah.
    BETTER ANSWER: Ac5s has 2/6; Ah5s has 2/4
  - [wrong] Ac5s has 2/4; Ah5s has 2/6 — Look again. It is the suited ace that removes the two calls.
    BETTER ANSWER: Ac5s has 2/6; Ah5s has 2/4

===== WORLD 25 · LESSON nut_blocker_and_unblocker · Nut blocker and unblocker =====

TASK w25_2_teach [theory] Which effect helps a candidate with zero showdown value?
CAPTION: Favor a river bluff that removes calls and leaves folds available, if its remaining fold share pays for the bet. A blocker cannot create a fold from a holding that still calls.
TEACH: Which effect helps a candidate with zero showdown value? Favor a river bluff that removes calls and leaves folds available, if its remaining fold share pays for the bet. A blocker cannot create a fold from a holding that still calls.
Q: Which effect helps a candidate with zero showdown value?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
  + [correct] It removes better hands that would call — Correct. Removing calls increases the fold share if the fold group is unchanged.
  - [wrong] It removes hands that would fold — Look again. That shrinks the reward branch.
    BETTER ANSWER: It removes better hands that would call
  - [wrong] It removes its own weakest kicker — Look again. Only actual removals from the defender’s legal response determine this comparison.
    BETTER ANSWER: It removes better hands that would call

TASK w25_2_read_block_calls_leave_folds [drill] Which candidate leaves the higher fold share?
CAPTION: On Kh 9h 4h 7c 2s, equal-weight response sample is call AhQh, AhJh, QhJh and fold AcKc, KsJd, KdJc. The exercise compares equally weak showdown candidates Ah5d and Ac5d as bluffs at the same size.
Q: Which candidate leaves the higher fold share?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
  + [correct] Ah5d — Correct. It removes two calls and leaves all three folds.
  - [wrong] Ac5d — Look again. It blocks AcKc, one of the holdings you need to fold.
    BETTER ANSWER: Ah5d
  - [wrong] The same — Look again. One ace conflicts with calls and the other conflicts with a fold.
    BETTER ANSWER: Ah5d

===== WORLD 25 · LESSON bluff_catcher_unblocking · Bluff catcher unblocking =====

TASK w25_3_teach [theory] What can make a same-rank bluff catcher worse?
CAPTION: When a river hand beats only bluffs, preserve combinations the opponent can bluff and remove combinations that beat you. Apply the price to that conditional range.
TEACH: What can make a same-rank bluff catcher worse? When a river hand beats only bluffs, preserve combinations the opponent can bluff and remove combinations that beat you. Apply the price to that conditional range.
Q: What can make a same-rank bluff catcher worse?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
  + [correct] Its suit blocks common misses — Correct. That leaves more value among the remaining bets.
  - [wrong] Its suit blocks strong value — Look again. Fewer strong bets can improve the bluff catcher.
    BETTER ANSWER: Its suit blocks common misses
  - [wrong] Its kicker is lower, with no change to the opposing range or wins — Look again. Only interactions with the board and opponent range matter.
    BETTER ANSWER: Its suit blocks common misses

TASK w25_3_read_read_draw_unblock [drill] Which keeps all listed misses available?
CAPTION: River Kd 8h 4h 7c 2s. BB’s modeled misses are AhQh, QhJh and JhTh. Compare KsQc and KsQh.
Q: Which keeps all listed misses available?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
  + [correct] KsQc — Correct. Qc conflicts with none of the three specified misses.
  - [wrong] KsQh — Look again. Qh removes AhQh and QhJh.
    BETTER ANSWER: KsQc
  - [wrong] Both — Look again. A queen of different suit changes the available heart draws.
    BETTER ANSWER: KsQc

===== WORLD 25 · LESSON paired_and_connected_removal · Paired and connected removal =====

TASK w25_4_teach [theory] What is the useful first step on a connected board?
CAPTION: Board texture tells you which strong hands to count. On a paired board count boats and quads; on a connected board identify the actual straight ranks before looking at your cards.
TEACH: What is the useful first step on a connected board? Board texture tells you which strong hands to count. On a paired board count boats and quads; on a connected board identify the actual straight ranks before looking at your cards.
Q: What is the useful first step on a connected board?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
  + [correct] List the holdings that actually make the target straight — Correct. That tells you which hole cards remove the hands you care about.
  - [wrong] Start by counting the suited connector classes — Look again. Many will not complete the relevant straight.
    BETTER ANSWER: List the holdings that actually make the target straight
  - [wrong] Treat an overcard as a nut blocker — Look again. Find the nut construction first.
    BETTER ANSWER: List the holdings that actually make the target straight

TASK w25_4_day7_four_flush_rank [review] Which hand has an ace-high flush?

CAPTION: Board Qh 9h 6h 4h 2c. Compare holding Ah and holding As with an offsuit non-heart kicker.

HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
REASONING: principle board_changes_strength · alt alternative · edge processRule · stack_matters false · assumption Board Qh 9h 6h 4h 2c. Compare holding Ah and holding As with an offsuit non-heart kicker.
  + [correct] Ah with the non-heart kicker — Correct. The ace of hearts joins the four board hearts.
  - [wrong] As with the non-heart kicker — Look again. The spade cannot supply a fifth heart.
    BETTER ANSWER: Ah with the non-heart kicker

===== WORLD 26 · LESSON chip_to_prize · Chip to prize =====

TASK w26_1_teach [theory] How do you compare an all-in call and a fold on the bubble?

TEACH: How do you compare an all-in call and a fold on the bubble? ICM converts a stack distribution into finish probabilities by allocating places in proportion to remaining chips. A static ICM decision compares payoffs after each branch of the hand.

HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
  + [correct] Weight the resulting prize equity of each branch — Correct. Changing the stack vector changes the prize distribution even when the chip gain looks favorable.
  - [wrong] Compare chips won instead of prize equity — Look again. The payout schedule assigns a different value to survival.
    BETTER ANSWER: Weight the resulting prize equity of each branch
  - [wrong] Use the min-cash amount as the payout estimate — Look again. A surviving stack retains chances of higher finishes.
    BETTER ANSWER: Weight the resulting prize equity of each branch

===== WORLD 26 · LESSON bounty_and_satellite · Bounty and satellite =====

TASK w26_5_teach [theory] When does a knockout bounty belong in a call comparison?

TEACH: When does a knockout bounty belong in a call comparison? Bounties add a reward for covered eliminations. Satellites instead value a qualifying seat. Convert all relevant outcomes into compatible prize units before comparing actions.
Q: When does a knockout bounty belong in a call comparison?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
  + [correct] On branches where you actually eliminate the target and receive it — Correct. Weight those branches and combine with the regular prize payoff in the same units.
  - [wrong] On the call itself, before knowing the result — Look again. A losing call gives no knockout reward.
    BETTER ANSWER: On branches where you actually eliminate the target and receive it
  - [wrong] Subtract the whole bounty from the chip price — Look again. Chip amounts and cash prizes are different units.
